    3  """What a trial actually cost, computed the same way for every contestant.
    4  
    5  **Why not just use what the agents report.** Each agent prices its own run from
    6  its own table, and the tables disagree. Measured on one identical task: Claude
    7  Code reported ``$0.3326`` and Stella ``$0.0641``. Stella's catalog knows the
    8  model, so its figure was a fair estimate; Claude Code's does not, so it priced
    9  GLM as the Anthropic model whose alias it had been pointed at. Read side by
   10  side that says "5x cheaper", which is not a fact about either agent — it is two
   11  pricing tables being subtracted from each other.
   12  
   13  So ArenaBench does not subtract self-reports. It takes the *token counts*,
   14  which both agents report accurately, and applies **one** table to both. That is
   15  the only way a cost column answers the question an operator is actually asking:
   16  same work, same prices, who spent less.
   17  
   18  **A subscription does not change the arithmetic.** On a coding plan the
   19  marginal spend is zero and no per-token comparison exists; what this computes
   20  is list-price equivalent — what the same tokens would have cost on metered
   21  billing. That is a real and useful number ("this run would bill $X"), and it is
   22  labelled as such rather than presented as an invoice.
   23  
   24  **An unpriced model gets no number, not a guessed one.** That is the whole
   25  lesson of the paragraph above: a plausible wrong figure populates a column,
   26  sorts against the other arm, and crowns a winner on a dimension nobody
   27  measured. Missing is strictly better than wrong here.
